kadoban · Oct 17, 2026

The model they're running is Qwen 3.8 27b. It's maybe somewhere around Opus 4.6 level, it's quite good. I didn't check the benchmarks, that's from memory/vibes.

The ~issue is though that they're using a pretty low quant, 2 bit. 4 bit are _pretty_ close to full ability, maybe degraded a bit. 2 bit is _noticably_ worse. It's about as small of a quant as you can get while still pretending it works, for this model.

This won't replace claude for you, unless you baby it a lot and are okay with it being kind or derpy.

thombles · Oct 17, 2026

Qwen3.8-27B is surprisingly effective, somewhere in the vicinity of Opus 4.6, but it needs to do a lot of inference-time computation. i.e. anything moderately involved requires xhigh reasoning and it will spend literally tens of thousands of tokens turning over a problem before emitting the answer. The answer/code/whatever is often surprisingly good, but if you’re in the low tens of tok/s you’ll be waiting a long time to get it.

As sibling said, you won’t hit the same quality using a 2 bit quant like this project, which is unfortunate but that’s the reality today.

GuB-42 · Oct 17, 2026

It is just a git repository. Sure, you may lost some issues if it is stuck down and no one made a backup, but the important part, the code is now spread all over the internet. Should they want to migrate, all they need is to ask those who used GitHub as the origin to do a "git remote origin set-url".

That's one of the best things with git (among with other DVCSs), it is incredibly resilient. I remember during an interview of Linus Torvalds about backups, he says he doesn't backup his work in the traditional sense, he has no real reason to when everything he does is copied millions of time.

The real point of GitHub for such a project is because GitHub is really popular, and it has a social network aspect to it. So yes, you are going to lose it if you get kicked out of GitHub, but by choosing a lesser known platform you won't get it in the first place. Also, their website is not on GitHub, so kicking them out of GitHub won't make them disappear completely.

Even though it only runs qwen 3.8 27b at a 2 bit quant, it's still highly viable, especially for things where you just need a constant token stream of slightly below average intelligence, ie this would be great for things like:

- monitoring server error rates

- reviewing security footage

- watching plant growth / controlling watering

etc. Any long running task you can now just slap a PS5 on it. 70 cents a day in power cost means you now get ~2M output tokens per day (~$3.50 worth of usage). It's not the worst thing in the world if you have one lying around. 2bit isn't even that terrible - it's ~80% the accuracy of 27b at full quant, which should put it at around GPT-5 levels of intelligence (which honestly is crazy in its own right).
